Library

Every book the planner knows about. The switch on a row says whether the planner uses that book; turning one off deletes nothing. The checkbox selects rows so you can act on several at once, and raises a bar with Remove in it. Removing is the only thing here that deletes.

Update data pulls the current 5etools release straight from the public repository. The app checks for a newer release when it opens. If the repository moves, edit its address under Actions → 5etools address.

Or load a 5etools data export yourself from ＋ Add files: the .zip, the unzipped folder, individual JSON files, or pasted JSON. Everything is parsed and stored in this browser. Nothing is uploaded.

Homebrew and Unearthed Arcana work too. Download a brew as JSON from the 5etools homebrew repository (D&D Beyond drops live there), or UA from the prerelease repository . They run around 60 KB each. A cloned repository scans fine as a folder: it is filed by category (spell/, class/, collection/), so one brew's content scatters across folders and the list below is how you find it. Do not use the repository's “Download ZIP”: that is every brew plus artwork, gigabytes no browser tab can open.

This planner ships without spell data. Load a 5etools data export to fill it with spells, classes, subclasses, feats and species. Everything is parsed and stored in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

The files you just added and the books they hold. A tick means add this book to my data. A book you already have is re-read rather than duplicated, and only identical entries are replaced; it is listed above the ticks, not among them. To remove a book you have, use the list's own selection bar.

Nothing is written until you press Add. Your builds are never touched.

Nothing imported yet. Adding these puts the app's built-in books behind them.

The 5etools mirror moves every year or two. If fetching stops working, put the new owner/repository here. Empty means the default above.

Print / save as PDF

The sheet is your spell table, under a line that says whose it is. These settings are remembered.

The file's name and its clickable spell links come from your browser's own PDF export. Chrome and Safari honour both. Some in-app PDF writers ignore them and save the page under the app's name; open this page in a browser to print if that happens.

Custom spell source

Something this character owns that grants spells: a magic item, a boon or a blessing.

Choose a spell

Pick the slot you want to fill, then click one of this build's own spells: it moves to that slot and whatever sat there shifts one later. Nothing is ever removed.

Clicking a spell records the trade. The one you replace keeps its place in the acquisition order, so every earlier level still reads the same.
